# Documentation invariants: prose that is a standing operator
# instruction, and the files that must keep saying it (#579).
#
# WHAT THIS FILE IS FOR
#
# Some documentation is reference material — it describes what the
# current version does, and it is supposed to change when the code
# changes. Gates already cover that kind: check-docs-drift.sh judges
# counters and settings, check-option-docs.sh judges driver-opts,
# check-version-pins.sh judges image pins.
#
# A different kind of documentation is a PRECONDITION. It tells the
# operator to do something before the software will work at all, it is
# true on every host and every version, and it is not made stale by a
# release. Nothing gates that kind, because there is no code fact to
# reconcile it against — and it is exactly the text a release
# documentation pass deletes in good faith, because it mentions an old
# version and therefore reads as changelog prose.
#
# This file is the reconciliation target such text does not otherwise
# have. Deleting a block listed here goes red, and the entry says why
# it must not be deleted, to whoever is holding the delete key.
#
# WHAT IT DOES NOT DO
#
# It cannot judge whether the prose is still CORRECT — only that it is
# still THERE. An invariant whose underlying behaviour has genuinely
# changed must be removed from this file in the same commit that
# removes it from the docs, and the gate going red is the prompt to
# make that a decision instead of a side effect.
#
# FORMAT
#
#   <invariant-id>
#       file: <path relative to the repo root>      (one or more)
#       marker: <literal substring>                 (one or more)
#       <justification, indented, one or more lines>
#
# Entries are separated by blank lines. Every entry needs at least one
# file, at least one marker, and a justification: an entry with no
# reason becomes a line somebody deletes along with the block it
# protects. Same rule as .github/linkadd-accounting.txt and
# .github/vuln-allowlist.txt.
#
# Markers are matched as fixed strings against SINGLE LINES, so pick
# something that cannot be re-wrapped: a command, or a short heading
# fragment. The same sentence is wrapped differently in each of the
# three files below, which is precisely why a marker must not be a
# sentence.

state-dir-bind-source
    file: README.md
    file: docs/index.md
    file: docs/reference.md
    marker: sudo mkdir -p /var/lib/net-dhcp
    marker: DO THIS FIRST
    v1.5.0 was the first release to bind-mount STATE_DIR from the host
    so leases survive an upgrade, and Docker will not create a missing
    bind source. The operator must create the directory BEFORE
    `docker plugin install`, on every host, new install or upgrade,
    indefinitely.
    Skip it and the install fails at start-up and leaves the plugin
    installed but disabled — after which re-running the identical
    command answers only "plugin ... already exists", which says
    nothing about the cause. A first-run experience with no path to
    the answer, and no error message anywhere that names the missing
    directory.
    The block reads like changelog prose because it names a version,
    and that is the trap: the version records when the behaviour
    landed, not when the instruction expires. It does not expire. It
    was kept by hand during the v1.6.0 documentation review; this
    entry is what replaces the reviewer having to know.
    Both markers are required in all three files. The heading alone
    could survive while the command is dropped, and the command alone
    could survive without the warning that makes anyone read it.
